# Public transcription eval corpus

A small corpus that any developer can run without private recordings. It is a
public smoke and tuning set (`split: "tune"`, `provenance: "synthetic"`), never
release holdout evidence.

## Running it

Run `yarn build` first, then use `scripts/mock.env.example` plus a real
`OPENAI_API_KEY`, as for the other evals. The 43 cases exceed the runner's 25-case batch cap, so a full run is two
invocations. Cases are sorted by id: batch 0 holds the `cut`, Japanese and normal
LibriSpeech cases, batch 1 the non-speech, long-pause, quiet, short and `tts-*`
cases. A report's `complete` covers its batch only; `selection.totalSelectedCases`
shows the full count.

```powershell
npm run eval:transcription -- --manifest test/fixtures/transcription-public/manifest.json --mode pipeline --pass-mode slow --runs 1 --batch-index 0
npm run eval:transcription -- --manifest test/fixtures/transcription-public/manifest.json --mode pipeline --pass-mode slow --runs 1 --batch-index 1
```

Dictionary terms are sent as recognition keywords, as in production; each
`tts-*` case sends its own case `dictionary`, so `byTag["dictionary-terms"]`
measures dictionary support. `--no-keywords` runs without them, as the
no-dictionary baseline. No prompt is sent unless `--prompt-file` passes one, and
no language hint unless `--language` forces one. `ja-fleurs-1607` is scored by
`cer`, outside the pooled `wer`.

## Contents

- `manifest.json` (43 cases): eight normal LibriSpeech utterances, two attenuated
  by 35 dB (`quiet`), three naturally short utterances, sixteen 1-4 word cuts of
  0.7-2.1 s (`cut`, three from the start of an utterance and thirteen added to
  measure language detection on short English speech), two utterances joined
  by 4 s of silence (`long-pause`), one Japanese FLEURS utterance and seven
  generated non-speech clips (silence, low and moderate noise, a 0.5 s noise burst, mains hum,
  keyboard-like clicks, a breath-like swell), plus five synthetic sentences
  full of made-up dictionary terms (`tts-*`, tag `dictionary-terms`), three of them
  mixed with pink noise.
- `familyId` groups cases derived from one source utterance (a `cut` shares its
  parent's family) and the `tts-*` cases of one made-up server.
  `speakerDeviceProfileId` names the reader or synthetic voice.
- The manifest `dictionary` is the made-up server's twenty terms. Each `tts-*`
  case carries its own made-up server's terms (eight or nine) as a case
  `dictionary`.
- `glossary-prompt.txt`: a made-up server glossary in the former production
  prompt template, also stored as the manifest `prompt`. Production sends no
  prompt; pass it with `--prompt-file` to reproduce the former prompted path.
  Nine of its dictionary terms occur in the speech references (twelve occurrences).
- `terms-prompt.txt`: the dictionary terms alone. `no-prompt.txt`: empty. Pass
  either with `--prompt-file`.

Audio is 16 kHz mono Opus at 24 kbps. Every case records its source in
`label.notes`. `manifest.json` pins each file's SHA-256, and
`test/evals/transcriptionCorpus.test.ts` checks every pin.

## Sources and licences

- LibriSpeech dev-clean, speaker 1272, via the `hf-internal-testing/librispeech_asr_dummy`
  parquet. LibriSpeech is CC BY 4.0 (<https://www.openslr.org/12>); the underlying
  LibriVox recordings are public domain. References are the corpus transcripts,
  sentence-cased, with `MISTER` written `Mr.` so that the usual ASR spelling is not
  counted as an error; that is the only change (for example `1272-128104-0003`
  reads `FREDERICK` in the corpus). Cut points for the `cut` cases came from local
  faster-whisper large-v3 word timestamps. The thirteen later cuts were kept only
  when faster-whisper large-v3 and large-v3-turbo both transcribed them as the
  corpus words, which favours clips current ASR gets right; they are tagged
  `asr-agreed` so the bias shows in `byTag`.
- FLEURS `ja_jp` dev id 1607, `google/fleurs` (CC BY 4.0). Reference is the raw
  corpus transcription.
- Non-speech clips are generated by ffmpeg `anullsrc`, `anoisesrc` and `aevalsrc`.
- `tts-*` sentences and their terms were written for this eval (fictional gaming
  guild and esports team names, codenames and given names from Irish, Polish,
  Nahuatl and Igbo). No customer term or audio is involved. Audio is OpenAI
  `gpt-4o-mini-tts` (voices coral, onyx, ash), the noisy ones mixed with ffmpeg
  `anoisesrc` pink noise, re-encoded to 16 kHz mono Opus. References are the
  synthesis input text.

All natural speech is one LibriSpeech reader plus one FLEURS reader, read speech
in quiet conditions. It is a smoke-level control, not a substitute for meeting audio.
